Unarmed-output goldens for the handoff-currency gate (D18 paired negative, spec 2026-09-08-handoff-currency-gate-design.md §Testing seams fixture 9). Captured 2026-09-08 by spawning the PRE-CHANGE hook (git show abc0876183:.claude/hooks/end-of-turn-reminder.sh) on every gate-fixture input with AIF_HANDOFF_GATE unset. The gate test replays these inputs against the EDITED hook and requires byte-identical stdout. Do not regenerate against an edited hook. Extended 2026-09-14 with f16/f17 (the D37 out-of-band /compact guard) captured from the SAME frozen abc0876183 hook; both are silent unarmed, which is the whole point of the paired negative.

f11-long-text-in-band re-captured twice on 2026-09-14 (recap-v2 slice 1): the branch payload text changed by design (D-A/D-B/D-C), first when the contract landed and again when the final whole-branch review restored the card's D-C sections. BOTH captures came from the same PRE-change hook (origin/staging dd2dd87b210) paired with the then-current lang packs, so the paired negative still compares an unedited hook against itself. The other 18 cases are untouched by either capture.

f11-long-text-in-band re-captured again on 2026-09-14 (recap-v2 slice 2, task 2.2): the shared recap contract gained the R-13 clause — when the fork card is already above in the same answer, section 3 of the block is ONE pointer line — so the only case whose expectedStdout embeds that contract moved, by exactly the three inserted lines. The capture again came from the PRE-change hook dd2dd87b210 paired with the new lang packs, and a 19-case replay confirmed this was the only case that moved.

f11-long-text-in-band re-captured once more on 2026-09-14 (recap-v2 slice 2, final whole-branch review finding I-1): section 3 of the contract listed the R-13 exception and then the full card template with no connector between them, so a model that had already emitted the card read "Then — as a card" first and the template last and would emit a second one. The fix appends "Otherwise — the card in full:" to the R-13 clause, moving f11 by exactly 32 bytes (3201 -> 3233). Captured from the same PRE-change hook dd2dd87b210 paired with the new lang packs; a 19-case replay confirmed f11 was the only case that moved.

Scope note on dd2dd87b210 (added 2026-09-14 after the slice-2 re-review, finding N-1): that sha is the pre-change hook with respect to the LANG PACKS only. Slice 2 merged origin/staging forward, which brought newer changes to .claude/hooks/end-of-turn-reminder.sh, so dd2dd87b210 is no longer the branch’s own hook. It stays a valid capture stand for a packs-only edit — verified by replaying all 19 cases against the live head hook as well, mismatches=0 — but a future capture must NOT reuse this sha blindly after a change to the hook itself: re-derive the frozen stand from the commit that precedes THAT change.

cases.expectedStdout:
{
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Stop. Before you finish — a recap in plain words, primarily for your own sake.

## 🟢 In plain words — a block of five sections, in this order:
1. **Where we are.** — always.
2. **What changed.** — if the answer is long or structural.
3. **Fork.** — if you are asking a question. Then — as a card. Inside this block
   the card omits its own 0 and 5: sections 1 and 5 of the block already own them.
   If the card is already above in this same answer — before the AskUserQuestion buttons, or one
   per question in an /arch round — section 3 is ONE pointer line to it, never a second card.
   One fork text per turn. Otherwise — the card in full:
   A fork is a card, not a bare question. In this order:
   0. Where we are — one sentence, no history.
   1. Title — the fork itself in everyday words.
   2. What we decide — with a concrete example from THIS project, never an analogy.
   3. If A — what becomes true. If B — what becomes true.
   4. ➡️ Recommendation — the MOST ESSENTIAL reason FIRST and in **bold**, then up to three
      more reasons, one line each; then one line: reversible or not, and what rolls it back.
   5. From you: ok — or "not ok, because …".
   Never compress the card: the line cap does not apply to it.
4. **What I am unsure about.** — optional.
5. **Next.** — always, and exactly two lines; the second one ends the block:
   Me: <what I am doing>
   From you: <one of four>
   — nothing (<what you would check, if you want to>)
   — waiting on: <what, from whom>
   — decide: <A> or <B>
   — do by hand: <one action>
Nothing else ever follows "From you:". The words
"проверь|ознакомься|убедись|посмотри|check that|review the|make sure|take a look" are not work for the human — they are offloading your own.
The whole block is no longer than 15 lines; the fork card does not count toward the cap.
Sentences in the block are short, at most 25 words. Split a long one in two instead of chaining clauses with colons, dashes and parentheses. Bad: "The test failed — the assert expected the old text (fixed it), green now". Good: "The test failed: the assert expected the old text. I fixed it. The test is green."
One idea per sentence. Bad: "Fixed X, but CI is red because of Y". Good: "Fixed X. CI is red: Y."
Write a CONTEXT.md term bare, as the glossary spells it, and never replace it with a paraphrase. Say jargon that is not in the glossary in plain words. Bad: "did a merge-forward". Good: "merged fresh staging into the branch".
What follows is not a block section and not in its cap — it is instructions to yourself:
• If in this turn you recommended something, or said "you decide" / "waiting for your call" / "PR is ready, awaiting your click" — check yourself: were the alternatives really weighed, or did you take the first that came to mind? If there is a clearly better option on the merits (by goals and discipline) — do NOT offload, do it and say what you did. Handing off a decision = reserved for real forks.
• The inverse: did you in this turn decide a fork SILENTLY — by a direct action/command/dispatch, without surfacing it as a question? If it is ambiguous (no clearly better option by the project's measures) — that is a silently-decided fork: surface it NOW via AskUserQuestion, do not leave it silently decided. The operator must see both open and closed forks.
• If the human asked this turn what a word means, explain it in the answer and, in the same turn, record it in CONTEXT.md: the definition plus their spelling under _Operator says_.

[context] This session's context is ≈ 320000 tokens (window ~1000000). If substantial judgment work (design, review, novel debugging) remains, write a short handoff note and continue it in a fresh session; if what is left is mechanical (commits, merges, regenerations guarded by external checks), finishing here is fine.",
  "systemMessage": "🎯 Gate fixture "
}
